claims.head: The Wild should tilt the ice
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Wild have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Sharks one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Wild’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve and has missed the last 6 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Collin Graf has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini.
Alexander Wennberg is on injured reserve and has missed the last 8 games. He is a top-six forward. Collin Graf has taken his spot beside Tyler Toffoli and Mason Marchment.
Filip Bystedt was added to the roster on Oct 29 and has played beside Tyler Toffoli and Ivar Stenberg.
Eric Pohlkamp was added to the roster on Nov 4.
Marcus Foligno is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.

Jared Spurgeon is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. Jonas Brodin has taken his spot beside Quinn Hughes. That pair has had 40% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 57:17 together, down from 69% with Spurgeon.

Brock Faber is on injured reserve (skull surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-pair defenseman. Jonas Brodin has taken his spot beside Quinn Hughes. That pair has had 61% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 162:43 together.

MIN.body: Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Sharks’ best way in is a power play that gets going.

story.head: The Wild should tilt the ice
paras: The Wild have won two in a row, while the Sharks are on a three-game losing streak. Going in, the Sharks are sixth in the Pacific (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Wild first in the Central (tied for second).

The Sharks’ record (.441) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.371), largely thanks to their goaltending. So is the Wild’s (.735 on chances worth .665), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (3rd lowest), are one of the league’s most physical teams (3rd) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). San Jose has scored 2.53 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. As for the Wild, they leave the shooting to their forwards (3rd lowest) and draw more penalties than they take (3rd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). Minnesota has allowed 2.24 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Sharks. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Macklin Celebrini (6 G / 11 A / 17 P in 15 GP) leads the Sharks in scoring, with a point in six straight games against Minnesota. Kirill Kaprizov (15 G / 11 A / 26 P in 17 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is tied for fifth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games and seven goals in eight games against San Jose since 2023-24. Quinn Hughes (5 G / 17 A / 22 P in 17 GP) isn’t far behind, with eight points in his last five games.
Yaroslav Askarov (4-7-0 / .887 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to go for San Jose. Jesper Wallstedt (10-2-3 / .919 SV% in 15 GS) has been outstanding for Minnesota and is expected to start.
The Wild usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.

items.text: The Wild are newly without Jared Spurgeon, have been without Marcus Foligno since Oct 8, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
The Sharks have been without Igor Chernyshov and Alexander Wennberg for several games.
With Alexander Wennberg out, Collin Graf took nine faceoffs in the Sharks’ last game. He had been taking fewer than one a game.
Joel Eriksson Ek has five goals on chances worth about 9.5 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
